items.title: Strategy denominated in BTC (MSTR/BTC)
items.description: Strategy's share price measured in bitcoin (MSTR/BTC) since August 2020. It peaked at 0.005 BTC per share in November 2024 and was back to 0.0013 on November 20, 2026, closer to the 2022 low of 0.0006 than to the peak.
items.reason: Strategy now trades below the value of its 851,305 BTC and faces removal from the MSCI USA Index after November 30. This shows how much ground the stock has lost against bitcoin itself.

items.title: The yield curve: 10Y minus 2Y and 10Y minus 3M Treasury spreads (month-end)
items.description: The 10-year minus 2-year and 10-year minus 3-month Treasury spreads at each month end since 1992. In early November 2026 the 10Y-2Y spread was 0.38 points and the 10Y-3M spread 0.67 points, down from 1.09 at the end of September.
items.reason: Hot October core PCE has a December Fed hike all but priced in, and the 2s10s curve is near its flattest since March 2025. This puts today's curve in 30 years of context.

items.title: SpaceX capex ($bn)
items.description: SpaceX capital spending by year: $4.4bn in 2023, $11.2bn in 2024 and $20.7bn in 2025, with estimates of $85.8bn in 2026 and a peak of $398.2bn in 2027 before easing to $174.4bn by 2030.
items.reason: The FCC just authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers. This is the spending bill behind that kind of ambition.

items.title: Tesla drawdowns from its record close vs the Nasdaq-100
items.description: Tesla's drawdown from its record close next to the Nasdaq-100's, weekly since 2019. As of November 6, 2026, Tesla was 26.9% below its record and the Nasdaq-100 13.6% below; Tesla's worst was -72.4% in January 2023 and the Nasdaq-100's -35.5% in October 2022.
items.reason: The Nasdaq-100 briefly fell 20% from its record on Wednesday before a late rally. This shows how Tesla's drawdowns usually run far deeper than the index's.

items.tab: 22 Big Tech unbooked leases by co
items.title: Signed, not yet on the books: data-center leases at Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet reached $830B (Jun 2026)
items.description: Data-center leases signed but not yet on the balance sheet at Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet. The total reached $830bn in June 2026, and by September Microsoft had $364.6bn, Meta $355.7bn, Amazon $164.9bn and Alphabet $130.5bn, up from about $208bn combined in December 2024.
items.reason: With Nvidia down again and on S&P credit watch, the AI selloff has investors asking what Big Tech is locked into. These off-balance-sheet commitments keep growing.
